Mr. M.M. Haque Siddique Rana, Advocate ------- For the opposite parties.
parties:
AKBAR ALI @ MD. AKBAR ALI AND OTHERS
Vs.
REASUDDIN BEING DEAD HIS LEGAL HEIRS 1(A) 
MD. ANWAR HOSSAIN AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
Khizir Ahmed Choudhury, J: This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 02.8.2001 passed by learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh in Other Class Appeal No.86 of 1999 affirming the order dated 26.1.1999 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Bhaluka, Mymensingh in Partition Suit No.47 of 1990 should not be set aside and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 2. The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Partition Suit being Partition Suit No.83 of 1981, being renumbered as Partition Suit No.47 of 1990. The present petitioners were defendant Nos. 57(gha) and 59 in the aforesaid suit. The suit was decreed ex-parte in preliminary form on 15.5.1996. The petitioner and another filed a written objection on 19.09.1995 against the report of the advocate Commissioner. Learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bhaluka by order dated 26.1.1999 rejected the written objection filed by the petitioner, accepted the reports submitted by advocate commissioner and subsequently drawn final decree on 08.3.1999. 

 3. The petitioner preferred Other Class Appeal No. 86 of 1999 before the District Judge, Maymensingh against the final decree and after hearing learned Subordinate Judge and Aurtho Rin Adalat, Maymensingh dismissed the appeal by judgment and order dated 02.8.2001 against which the instant rule. 

 4. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali along with Mr. Subrata Saha, learned advocates appeared for the petitioner. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali learned advocate submits that admittedly the petitioners are co-sharers in the suit land and the total quantum of suit land is 48.43 acres which plaintiffs claim is only 0.55 acres of land for which he got decree in preliminary form. He next submits that after allotting the share to the plaintiff vast tract of land remained as residuary shares and out of that some other defendants namely defendant Nos.94, 189, 190, 199, 73, 113, 111 obtained saham regarding 27.64 acres of land by filing an application, even though they did not submit any sorts of documents in support of their claim, but in spite of filing of relevant documents by the petitioner, the Court below did not consider the documents and objection and without adverting the same rejected the objection which caused failure of justice. He next submits that the appellate Court dismissed the appeal citing some technical ground regarding particular date being erroneously mentioned in the memo of appeal which is technical in nature. He next submits that before drawing up final decree the petitioner filed objection and as such it was incumbent upon the trial Court to consider the contents of the written objection and to direct the advocate commissioner to cause inquiry whether the petitioner is entitled to get his claimed saham from the residuary property, but the trial Court without any consideration rejected the same and drew final decree which caused failure of justice. Apart from this petitioner Nos. 2(a) 2(i) filed an application for allotment of saham in respect of 4.04 acres of land in favour of them. 

 5. Mr. M.M. Haque Siddique Rana, learned advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that after preliminary decree, the opposite party filed an application for appointment of advocate commissioner for demarcating his land and accordingly advocate commissioner went to the locality and thereafter allotted specific saham to the plaintiff opposite party and consequently the trial Court has drawn final decree in pursuance of the commissioner's report and as such the present approach of the petitioner for allotting saham to them from residuary property is not sustainable. He next submits that since the petitioner did not contest the suit in spite of service of summons, their share has not been allotted by the Court and as such they are not entitled to get any share by filing belated application. 

 7. It appears from the findings of the learned Assistant Judge that the petitioner did not raise objection against the ex-parte judgment and decree and specifically did not raise any particular objection regarding the commissioner's report and the petitioner also took no step against the ex-parte judgment and decree whereby suit land has been ordered to be partitioned, consequently learned Assistant Judge by the same order drawn final decree. The appellate Court held that the any infirmity in the trial Court's judgment regarding preliminary decree cannot be considered at the time of hearing of objection regarding the report filed by the commissioner. The appellate Court also held that in the memo of appeal order dated 13.1.1999 has been challenged but in fact the impugned order has been passed on 26.1.1999 and as such from that count also the appeal is not maintainable. 

 11. On perusal of the decisions as referred by the learned advocate of the opposite party it appears that before final decree any share can be allotted to the co-sharer in spite of his not having contested to the original suit, if he can prove his title and possession over any residuary shares of any partible property but after pronouncement of final decree there is little scope to consider any co-sharer's claim regarding allotment of share out of residuary ejmali property. In the case of Alekjan Bewa and others vs. Alefa Bewa and others reported in 7 ADC 593, Aziz Ahmed and another vs. Khorsheda Begum alias Monwara Begum and others reported in 7 MLR AD 25, Md. Atar Ali Sheikh and others vs. Md. Karam Ali Sheikh and others reported in 11 BLT 44 similar views are reiterated by our apex Court. 

 12. Total partible land is 48.43 acres out of which plaintiffs claim is only 0.55 acres which has been allotted to him by the Advocate Commissioner and accordingly, final decree has been drawn up. Another 27.94 acres of land has been allotted to other defendant from residuary shares. Apart from the allotted shares still there remained residuary property wherefrom the present petitioners are claiming 15.79 acres of land. In the application for allotting saham the petitioner submitted certain photoset copies of the document in support of their claim. On perusal of the documents it appears that those are old and ancient one but its veracity cannot be ascertained because of having not formally proved. But since residuary shares still remains, the genuineness of the documents and other aspects should be investigated without upsetting the share and possession allotted to the plaintiff opposite party as well as the defendant opposite parties to whom specific shares have been allotted as per showing of the Advocate Commissioner. The trial Court can depute the said Advocate who held investigation regarding the suit land allotting the shares to the plaintiff and other defendants and if, the said advocate commissioner is not available or found absent another advocate commissioner can be deputed for considering petitioners claim out of residuary properties. But before that the petitioners are required to submit all title deeds and other required papers in original or in absence of originals by producing certified copies with due explanation thereof, for making proper inquiry regarding the claim of the petitioner and as such final decree passed by the trial Court is required to be set aside as because keeping the final decree intact inquiry cannot be held regarding the title and other aspect of the petitioners claim. 

 13. In the above context, the final decree dated 26.01.1999 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Bhaluka, Maymensingh and the judgment and decree dated 02.8.2001 passed by erstwhile Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh are hereby set aside. The shares allotted to the plaintiff-opposite parties and the defendant-opposite parties by the Advocate Commissioners report as well as possession will remain intact. If any further commission is held and after examining and scrutinizing the documents submitted by the petitioners if the petitioners are entitled to get any share from residuary properties it cannot anyway affect the plaintiff opposite parties share and possession as well as the defendant opposite parties share and possession which they have got meanwhile.
